clue.text: Refuse to get central heating in sub-office

parts.note: bran is the husk left over from milling grain, so a kind of refuse or waste
CH is the usual abbreviation for central heating in property listings

explanation.surface: Someone declines to have central heating installed in a small local office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb (to decline) but is the noun, waste matter, here bran.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch is a subsidiary office of a bank or firm, standing under the head office.

clue.text: Attractive Beatrice, attentive, ousting daughter

parts.note: Bea is a short form of the name Beatrice

indicators.note: ousting means the daughter's letter is thrown out

parts.note: dutiful means attentive to one's duties
D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies

explanation.surface: Beatrice is a lovely, considerate girl who has pushed her daughter aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ousting' removes D from DUTIFUL to leave UTIFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Beautiful and attractive are synonyms for good-looking.

clue.text: Fleet runner has edge in East European car when reversing

indicators.note: reversing means the assembled letters are read backwards, as a car goes backwards
in places the edge within the car's name

parts.note: Lada is a Russian make of car
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A Russian motorist scrapes an edge while backing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet runner' suggests a sprinter but is the commander of a fleet. 'when reversing' turns the whole container round, as a car backs up.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral commands, or runs, a fleet of warships.

clue.text: Study sure-fire winner: two pieces of Grieg with piano

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a cert is a racing certainty, a sure winner

indicators.note: two pieces of takes the first two letters of the composer's name

parts.note: and means with, joining things together

explanation.surface: A pianist studies two Grieg works that are sure to win a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two pieces of' takes GR, the first two letters of 'Grieg'.
explanation.definitionFit: A concert grand is the largest kind of grand piano, built for concert halls.

clue.text: A shudder, mostly, when honour

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'A shudder, mostly, when honour', has no reversal indicator for TREMO(R) and no full definition of the silent code; the OCR text appears cut short and no search found the printed words.

clue.text: Airy doctor bagging starts of lung operations

indicators.note: bagging means the doctor holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a medic is a doctor

indicators.note: starts of picks the first letters of lung and operations

explanation.surface: A breezy surgeon takes on the beginnings of chest procedures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts of' gives L and O; 'bagging' puts them inside MEDIC. 'Airy' means having an air, a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune, so something tuneful or melodious is airy in that sense.

clue.text: Some clearer unanimity required — a second vote?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A clearer consensus is needed, so the ballot must be held again.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is in 'cleaRER UNanimity'. The draft definition also took 'required', but it is a link: the definition is just 'a second vote'.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeat of an election or ballot is held a second time.

clue.text: Mediaeval science student enthralled by pain-gosh!

indicators.note: enthralled by means the student is held inside the pain

parts.note: an ache is a pain
L is a learner, from the L-plates on a learner driver's car
my! is an exclamation of surprise like gosh!

explanation.surface: A student caught up in a painful subject exclaims in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner comes from the L-plates British learner drivers display; 'enthralled by' puts L inside ACHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval alchemists sought to turn base metals into gold, a precursor of chemistry.

clue.text: One research area set up in exotic location

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a lab is where research is done

explanation.surface: A single research facility has been established somewhere exotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns I + LAB round, as a down entry reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indonesian island is a classic faraway holiday destination.

clue.text: Almost everyone preparing for war? That's worrying

indicators.note: almost means the word for everyone loses its final letter

parts.note: all means everyone
arming is equipping troops for war

explanation.surface: A whole nation getting ready for conflict is a worrying sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alarming causes worry or fear, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Vicar, say, left in church, not entirely wealthy

indicators.note: in places the letter for left within the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: not entirely means the word for wealthy loses its last letter

parts.note: rich means wealthy

explanation.surface: A clergyman left in his church is only moderately well off.
explanation.walkthrough: CE is the Church of England, the national church. 'not entirely' cuts the H from RICH.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is one example of a clergyman, hence the 'say' marking an example.

clue.text: Bargain supply of matches?

parts.note: the matches are sporting fixtures, not things to strike, and a pass bought for a whole year of them is cheaper than paying at the gate each time

explanation.walkthrough: 'matches' suggests boxes of matches; it means football games, entry to all of which comes in one advance purchase.
explanation.definitionFit: A pass covering every home game of a sporting year costs less than buying entry match by match.

clue.text: Co-operation without head of NATO is ridiculous pretence, indeed

indicators.note: ridiculous suggests the letters are absurdly jumbled into a new order
head of picks the first letter of the alliance's name

explanation.surface: Without a NATO leader, alliance co-operation is a ridiculous sham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is ridiculous' rearranges N (head of NATO) with PRETENCE and INDEED; 'without' is a link here, meaning the letter comes along outside the printed fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutual dependence between parties is a form of working together.

clue.text: A fellow faults dodgy inspiration

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or suspect, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A college fellow finds questionable inspiration in his mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' rearranges FAULTS to FLATUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Afflatus is divine or creative inspiration, the breath of a muse.

clue.text: Copper's shot — quite safe

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper; the 's is a link meaning 'has'
a shy is a throw or attempt, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: A policeman has fired a gun, but nobody is in danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the element, chemical symbol CU. A coconut shy is a British fairground stall where you throw balls at coconuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushy job is easy and comfortable, free of risk or hardship.

clue.text: Certainly upset -ranted awfully inside (though not really activated)

indicators.note: inside means the jumbled word goes within the turned-round word
in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: yes means certainly

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone certainly upset ranted dreadfully, though not actually moved to act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the word for certainly round, and the anagram from 'awfully' sits 'inside' it. The definition is in brackets as an aside: someone who sits about is not moved to act.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedentary person sits a lot and takes little exercise.

clue.text: Very religious group to provide guide

parts.note: pi is informal for pious, very religious
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: A devout congregation offers to lead someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilot something is to steer or direct it, the same as guiding it.

clue.text: Letters received after game?

parts.note: post is Latin for after, as in postwar
a bag is the game killed in a shoot

explanation.surface: Fan mail arrives once a match is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like a match but is the hunter's sense, animals shot, the day's bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A postbag is the mail a person or publication receives.

clue.text: Allowed to pick up car in Midland town

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: let means allowed
a Ford is a make of car

explanation.surface: Someone is permitted to collect a vehicle in a Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pick' is a link. The Midlands is the central region of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Telford is a new town in Shropshire, in the English Midlands.

clue.text: Circles reduced plan for part of boxing arena

parts.note: rings are circles

indicators.note: reduced means the word for plan is shortened by its last letter

parts.note: an idea is a plan

explanation.surface: Scaled-down circular designs for a boxing venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' clips the last letter from IDEA. 'Circles' looks like a verb but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringside is the area immediately around a boxing ring, where the closest spectators sit.

clue.text: Is' isle a slip for land-locked area?

indicators.note: a slip is an error, so the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Is calling it an island a mistake for a region with no coast?
explanation.walkthrough: 'a slip' signals that IS, ISLE and A are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Silesia is a historical region of central Europe, mostly in Poland, far from the sea.

clue.text: Odd sand hill stands round end of groyne in Scottish area

indicators.note: round means the jumbled letters go around the other piece
odd means strange, so the letters are rearranged
end of picks the final letter of the word groyne

explanation.surface: A strange dune formation sits by a breakwater on the Scottish coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' is the anagram signal, not a description of the hill. A groyne is a low sea wall built out from a beach to stop sand drifting.
explanation.definitionFit: The archipelago north of mainland Scotland is a Scottish council region.

clue.text: English of reduced strength to produce excellent people

parts.note: lite describes a weaker or low-calorie version of a product

explanation.surface: A watered-down English brew makes for fine company.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the best of a group, its top people.

clue.text: Did for a good many

explanation.definitionFit: To do for someone is to kill them, as slew is the past tense of slay; a slew is also a large number.

clue.text: South coast resort gutted by country dweller

indicators.note: gutted means some of the insides of the resort's name are removed

parts.note: Brighton is a seaside town on England's south coast

explanation.surface: A seaside town ruined by someone from the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' removes GH from the middle of BRIGHTON, an English south-coast seaside town. 'country' means nation, not countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A Briton is an inhabitant of Britain, the nation in question.

clue.text: Heavenly view is top in Highland locale

indicators.note: in places the other pieces within the name of the island

parts.note: Skye is an island in the Scottish Highlands
's is a contraction of is
a cap is a top or lid

explanation.surface: The best view of the sky is found in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly' suggests something divine; here it just means of the sky. SKYE is an island off the Scottish Highlands coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A skyscape is a picture or panorama of the sky, so a view of the heavens.

clue.text: Eager end to trilling of an oboe?

indicators.note: end to takes the final letter of trilling

parts.note: an oboe is a reed instrument, so its sound is reedy

explanation.surface: A keen oboist ends a passage with a trill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end to' takes G from 'trilling'. An oboe's tone is described as reedy because it is played through a double reed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being greedy for something means being avid or hungry for it.

clue.text: Sexy group breaking bounds of salacity

indicators.note: breaking means the group splits apart the outer letters
bounds of means the first and last letters of salacity

parts.note: a team is a group

explanation.surface: A gang crashes through the limits of lewdness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bounds of' gives S and Y, the first and last letters of 'salacity'; 'breaking' puts TEAM between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamy scene is erotic, full of sexual heat.
